title: Bounded regression debt closure

fixes.root_cause_statement: cmd_start called _check_env() unconditionally before the readiness decision layer. _check_env required the repository-root .venv and saathi-os/node_modules — artifacts only the SPAWN paths consume. On any checkout without them, start aborted before it could reuse a healthy process or report a real blocker, and the operator was told the venv was missing when the actual blocker was an unhealthy or unrelated listener.
fixes.smallest_architectural_repair: Split _check_env into three scoped predicates. _check_env now covers only the host-level prerequisite every readiness probe needs (curl). _check_backend_toolchain (venv) is invoked from _ensure_backend on the `free` branch — the only branch that spawns uvicorn. _check_frontend_toolchain (node_modules) is invoked from _ensure_frontend on its `free` branch — the only branch that spawns `npm run dev`.
safety_preserved: Both spawn paths still abort non-zero with the identical remediation text when their toolchain is missing.
Fail-closed blockers for owned-unhealthy, external-unhealthy and unrelated listeners are unchanged.
No external process is killed; PID ownership logic untouched.
Localhost-only binding, lock file, and log redaction untouched.
safety_improved: The PID-safety refusal ('refusing to kill it') and the frontend BLOCKER message are now reachable and are reported as the actual reason for failure instead of being masked by a generic environment error.

fixes.root_cause_statement: prepare() aggregated the .venv and saathi-os/node_modules checks into `ok` as required host prerequisites. Because these are OUTPUTS of installation, prepare() could never return ok on a machine where installation had not already been performed in place, permanently blocking init_first_run() (PREPARE_FAILED), upgrade_preflight()/apply_local_upgrade() (PREFLIGHT_FAILED) and the M165 certification gate (installation_prepare FAIL).
fixes.smallest_architectural_repair: Introduce INSTALLABLE_CHECKS = ('python_venv', 'frontend_deps'). prepare()'s add() marks those entries installable=True and routes their FAIL status to a new deterministic field `install_complete` plus `pending_install_steps`, instead of clearing `ok`. `ok` continues to reflect every genuine host prerequisite. doctor(), init_first_run(), upgrade_preflight() and the M165 gate all propagate the new field; the gate gains an explicit `installation_complete` check so an incomplete install stays visible rather than being dropped.
safety_preserved: Both checks still run and still record status FAIL with their full detail text.
Both remediation strings ('python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e .[dev]', 'cd saathi-os && npm install') are still emitted.
init_first_run still hard-refuses when a host prerequisite fails (ok=False → PREPARE_FAILED).

The acknowledge_local_only gate, the 'no API credentials collected' posture, symlink rejection on required directories, disk-headroom gating, remote_fetch=false and production_authorized=false are all unchanged.
No check was deleted, downgraded to PASS, made non-required, or removed from the report.
safety_improved: The M165 certification report now distinguishes an unusable host from an un-installed one, so a genuinely failing prerequisite is no longer camouflaged by a permanently-red gate.

fixes.root_cause_statement: The gate counted any `private_key_block` rule hit as a strong credential leak. That rule matches the PEM header alone. Two security-control modules embed the header as intentional non-secret material — a rejection sample proving the payload sanitiser refuses private keys (broker_readiness/security.py:100) and a detector pattern definition (integration_assurance/security.py:114) — so the gate returned EXIT_SECURITY (3) on its own safety machinery. Its only exclusion was a tests/ and docs/ path prefix filter, which does not cover security-control source.
fixes.smallest_architectural_repair: Add pem_carries_key_material(): a private_key_block hit counts as a strong credential only when a base64 body of at least 100 characters follows the PEM header — the same materiality standard integration_assurance/security.py already applies. Non-material markers are recorded in the report under `non_material_markers` with an explicit reason rather than being silently dropped. Every other strong rule blocks unchanged.
why_this_is_not_a_weakening: A real PEM private key always carries a base64 body; a bare marker never does. Detection of real key material is unchanged.
No file, directory or module was added to an allowlist.
The tests/ and docs/ path exclusion was NOT widened — a test asserts the original exclusion expression is still present and that neither offending module name appears in the gate source.
The two excluded markers are reported in the gate output, so the exclusion is auditable rather than invisible.
An end-to-end regression test injects a credential-bearing hit and asserts the gate still returns EXIT_SECURITY.

byte_identity_check.method: git hash-object <file> compared to git rev-parse 6cdf726:<file>

proof_tests_were_not_weakened.conclusion: All three suites containing the eight inherited failures are byte-identical to the predecessor commit. Every failure was closed in implementation. 18 new focused regression tests were added in tests/test_m336_m343_regression_closure.py, each of which asserts a safety behaviour that the repair had to preserve.

authority_expansion_check.note: No new network, credential, provider, execution or deployment capability was introduced. All changes are local classification and reporting logic.

documentation_updated: docs/platform/M57_PROCESS_MANAGEMENT.md — Start section now describes the role-conditional toolchain preflight precisely.
